summary: Correct erfühlt to erfüllt in sense 2
rationale: The gloss concerns a Bedingung, Wunsch or Anliegen being fulfilled, not felt by touch. The entry itself translates u=šarṭ kaməl as “die Bedingung ist erfüllt”.

summary: Correct the consonant in taḥrə
rationale: The cited verse reads “ḥfəlle taḥte ḥḏo mad dawmanək di baxča”. The entry has r for the second t of taḥte. This is a consonant substitution, not a clitic-boundary or vowel normalization.

summary: Use hätte in the counterfactual result clause
rationale: The conditional “wenn deine Stunde da wäre” requires the counterfactual “hätte ... gebissen”; indicative hatte incorrectly makes it a past assertion.

summary: Restore the prefix of gəmkamannole
rationale: The supplied corpus reads “u waʕdawo gəmkamannole”. The glossary omits the gə- prefix of this verb rather than merely changing the clitic boundary or stress.

summary: Sense 4: revise the gloss
after: erwachsen, mannbar werden; ein bestimmtes Lebensalter erreichen;
rationale: Existing age-nineteen material and 95/26 (six/seven months, two years), 112/3 (sixty years) require age attainment beyond maturity.

summary: Completion contrasts intransitive I with active II: prayer/harvest/house become complete, while agents complete work, quantities or promises. Existing courage use is already sense II.2, so it is not duplicated as a new idiom.

Infectum-wa marks recurrent procedural completion (agriculture, construction, food) and conditional finishing-off in Lahdo; I Infectum-wa with time also supports an irrealis protasis in PrS 1/37. The suffix does not determine one discourse function.

Finite feminine kamilo must be distinguished from masculine Part act. kamilo by subject and clause structure: funeral prayer and elapsed year versus grown man or completed story. Arabic-shaped mətkamməl remains unassigned.
The I Preterit-wa is newly evidenced by the Farida mourning-period self-correction. L-marking with elapsed time can code the affected person; do not infer a transitive agent solely from -le.

PrS source and old entry citations differ (1/36 versus prs 3/24, 1/37 versus prs 3/25, 70/72 versus prs 199/37). The matching text warrants deduplication, not a citation replacement without edition concordance.
Confirm whether I kamilo predicates in oral closing formulas and object descriptions are productive Part act. or partly lexical Arabic adjectives; is PrS 64/23 uninflected kaməl a loan adjective?

Confirm reduced II imperative kamal/kamela (52/70,83,89) and whether PrS 45/35 kamele is reduced II or I with an L-suffix. Check gəmkamlalle (52/32) segmentation and 6/61 masculine -lux addressed to a wife.
MAC Besim History of Bsorino/47: is u+dayno the sum raised, the purchase obligation, or a repaid loan? The stated deficit and borrowing do not establish repayment.
Check singular agreement with quantified duration in PrS 38/23 and recurring kkoməl šato in PrS 86/22-23; preserve source wording.
At 93/22, does kamilo predicate completion of the ascent or the spatial end of its boundary? The spatial sense rests on this one attestation.

115/309 kemolo is proposed as Infinitiv on nominalized year-end usage. Its supplied translation has an alignment flag with additional dialogue absent from this verse; the translation has been withheld. Supply a verified aligned edition excerpt and confirm Infinitiv versus a lexical event noun.

At 112/64 kaməl yo seems serious/firm rather than a fulfilled request; at 112/77 clarify complete versus binding/valid. At 68/56 distinguish maturity from evaluative accomplishment; no new sense is accepted from translation alone.
Confirm that mi- mikaməl in Hors 3/22 / RT 22 is II Detransitive Infectum; Arabic mətkamməl at 102/45 is deliberately not used to establish Part. Pass.
Correct the German noun Tage
rationale: The German noun is Tage; ṭ is a transcription character accidentally used in the translation. The supplied edition has “Als drei Tage um waren”.

summary: Capitalize the German noun Schule
rationale: Schule is a German noun. The supplied edition reads “mit der Schule fertig”.

summary: Complete state extends to shaped objects, narrated stories, proposals and pledges; German richtig does not alone establish correctness.

summary: A horse is complete with its equipment (kamilo me kul mede); me introduces the inventory of completeness.
Attained age may be predicated of ʕəmr as subject or the person with an L-suffix; includes infancy and old age, now explicit in the gloss.
dayno occurs while making up a purchase shortfall after borrowing; debt repayment cannot be inferred from the English rendering.
